title: In-House vs Outsourcing Cost Calculator (Free)
description: Compare the full first-year cost of hiring an employee with outsourcing the same work. Add salary, on-costs, overheads and agency rates: free and private.
h1: Should you hire or outsource? Compare the real cost
intro: Salary is only part of the cost of an employee. Add on-costs, overheads and recruitment, then compare against a provider’s hourly rate or monthly fee.

blocks.html:
In-house vs outsourcing cost calculator

Enter your own figures. The calculator compares a year of employing someone with a year of buying the same work from a provider.

sections.h2: What to include in the in-house cost
sections.html:
• Employer on-costs: payroll taxes or National Insurance, social security, pension or 401(k) contributions, health insurance and other benefits. These vary by country, so use your own figures or ask your accountant.
  • Overheads: laptop, software licences, office space, training and management time.
  • Recruitment: agency fees, job ads and interview time.
  • Hidden time: holidays, sickness and the time it takes a new hire to get fully up to speed.

sections.h2: When outsourcing tends to make sense
sections.html:
• The work is specialist, occasional or seasonal.
  • You need it in a country where you don’t have a company.
  • You want to scale up or down quickly.
  • You need cover across several skills that one hire couldn’t provide.

When the work is core, constant and needs close day-to-day control, hiring often wins. Many businesses use a mix of both.
Use the project brief builder to request quotes, then plug the real numbers back in here.

faqs.q: Is the calculator accurate for my country?
faqs.a: It only uses the figures you enter, so it works in any country and currency. The accuracy depends on your inputs, especially employer on-costs, which differ by country.

faqs.q: Do you store what I type?
faqs.a: No. The calculation happens in your browser, and nothing is sent to us.
